Savings Calculator

A savings calculator determines the future accumulated balance of your bank savings account or emergency fund when regular contributions compound with interest over time. It can also reverse-calculate the exact monthly deposit required to reach a specific financial savings milestone (such as a house down payment or vacation fund) by a target deadline.
Interactive Savings CalculatorInstant In-Browser Calculation
Estimated Output
--

Formula and Calculation Method

Compound savings future value formula with regular monthly deposits:

FV = P × (1 + r/12)^(12t) + PMT × [((1 + r/12)^(12t) - 1) ÷ (r/12)]

Worked Example and Step-by-Step Calculation

Building a $30,000 Emergency Fund ($5,000 initial, $400/mo at 4.5% APY)
Input Values:
  • Starting Balance (P): $5,000
  • Monthly Deposit (PMT): $400
  • Annual Percentage Yield (APY): 4.5%
  • Timeline: 5 years (60 months)

1. Starting balance growth = $5,000 × (1 + 0.045/12)^60 = $6,258.98

2. Monthly deposits growth = $400 × [((1 + 0.045/12)^60 - 1) ÷ (0.045/12)] = $26,851.35

3. Total Future Balance = $6,258.98 + $26,851.35 = $33,110.33

4. Total Deposited = $5,000 + ($400 × 60) = $29,000 | Interest Earned: $4,110.33

Result: Total Saved: $33,110.33 in 5 years (Interest Earned: $4,110.33)

How to Use the Savings Calculator

  1. Enter your initial starting deposit balance.
  2. Enter your recurring monthly contribution amount.
  3. Input the annual interest rate (APY) offered by your savings account.
  4. Specify your saving timeframe in months or years.
  5. Instantly see your total balance, principal deposits, and cumulative interest earned.

Common Mistakes, Limitations & Practical Guidance

  • High-yield savings account APYs are variable and adjust when central bank benchmark interest rates change.
  • Annual bank interest income exceeding $10 is taxable and reported on IRS Form 1099-INT.

Frequently Asked Questions About Savings Calculator

How large should my emergency fund be?

Financial planners universally recommend maintaining 3 to 6 months of essential living expenses (rent, food, utilities, debt payments) in a liquid, FDIC-insured high-yield savings account to protect against unexpected job loss or medical events.

What is the difference between APR and APY in savings accounts?

APR (Annual Percentage Rate) is the simple interest rate before compounding is considered. APY (Annual Percentage Yield) reflects the actual total return earned over a full year, accounting for intra-year compound interest.

How does compound interest help my savings?

Compound interest generates interest on both your deposited principal and the prior interest you have already earned. Over time, interest payments steadily accelerate your balance growth without additional effort.

Are online high-yield savings accounts safe?

Yes, provided the institution is an FDIC-insured member bank (or NCUA-insured credit union). Your deposit balances are legally guaranteed by the federal government up to $250,000 per depositor.

How does this tool connect with the Budget Calculator?
